question: Lime water turns milky on passing carbon dioxide gas through it due to the formation of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**CaCO3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Limewater** is an alkaline solution made from **calcium hydroxide** that is **weakly soluble** in water.
 
• The production of **calcium carbonate** occurs when** carbon dioxide gas** is passed through or over limewater.
 
• Carbon dioxide combines with limewater (a calcium hydroxide solution, Ca(OH)₂) to generate a** white calcium carbonate** precipitate, CaCO₃.
 
• When **more carbon dioxide** is added, the precipitate dissolves, forming a **colourless calcium hydrogen carbonate solution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Ca(HCO3)****2** 

 
 
• **Calcium bicarbonate**, also called **calcium hydrogen carbonate,** has the chemical formula Ca(HCO₃)₂.
 
• It is a **white crystalline powder** that is **soluble** in water.
 
• It is used as a** food additive**, as an** anti-caking agent,** and as a** color stabilizer. **
 
• Calcium bicarbonate causes** the temporary hardness** of the water.
 
• Calcium bicarbonate solution in water has health benefits due to the** alkalizing effect and mineral content. **
 
 
 
• **​****CaO**
 
 
• Calcium oxide (CaO), commonly known as **quicklime or burnt lime**, is a widely used chemical compound.
 
• It is a **white, caustic, alkaline, crystalline solid** at room temperature.
 
• It is widely used in** industry**, e.g., in making porcelain and glass; in purifying sugar; in preparing bleaching powder, calcium carbide, and calcium cyanamide; in water softeners; and in mortars and cement. In agriculture, it is used for treating acidic soils (liming).
 
• It is an **amorphous white solid** with a melting temperature of **2600 degrees Celsius.**
 
• It's a compound that's** extremely stable** and can **resist high temperatures.**
 
• When it comes into contact with water, it becomes **slaked lime.**
 
• Calcium oxide is** ionic** because it is formed between a metal and non-metal.
 
 
 
• **Ca(OH)2**
 
 
• Calcium hydroxide is known as **slaked lime or hydrated lime**.
 
• Calcium oxide (also known as lime or quicklime) is blended or "slaked" with water to produce a **colourless crystal or white powder.**
 
• It can also be precipitated by combining an aqueous calcium chloride solution with an aqueous sodium hydroxide solution.
 
• A suspension of fine calcium hydroxide particles in water is called **milk of lime.** 
 
• It turns milky if carbon dioxide is passed through, due to the precipitation of **calcium carbonate.**
